messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: PagerDuty PD-14 fired — prometheus scrape errors for cluster prod-west (targets going UNKNOWN / scrape timeout). Auto-escalation in 3m if not acknowledged :rotating_light:
pagerduty: PagerDuty: PD-14 assigned to oncall: alice — please acknowledge.
alice: acked. I'm oncall, looking now. ping me with any quick facts. :pray:
dave: saw this spike at ~10:06Z, kubelet targets showing 503s and TLS handshake failures. Looks like a node-level networking flap affecting node-exporter endpoints. Logs from prom-scraper: ```WARN: scrape failed for job=node-exporter/10.2.14.7:443: read tcp 10.5.0.12:443: i/o timeout```
ben: also seeing many missing series for job="kubelet" and job="node-exporter" in the service map. grafana alert for scrape_failure_ratio tripped.
cara: customer-facing note: model-serving tail latency is rising on a few routes but not widespread; looks like ingestion metrics missing rather than actual model degradation. Still, we should flag potential downstream alerts.
alice: good call. Are logs ingest/backpressure showing any backlog? ops-bot can you dump ingest-lag?
ops-bot: log-ingest: write-buffer-latency spikes on ingest-pipeline-3: 12s -> 82s over last 5m. ingestion-queue-length=1200. No backfill job currently running.
dave: kubelet node-exporter pods on node pool "gpu-prod-2" show CrashLoopBackOff on a couple nodes. suspect kernel OOM killer restarted node-exporter; checking dmesg.
ben: if node-exporter crashed, prometheus will mark targets as DOWN -> scrape failures. Two quick mitigations: 1) scale prom-scraper replicas so remaining scrapers can pick up targets, 2) restart node-exporter daemonset on affected nodes. Which do we prefer?
alice: do both in parallel. I'll scale prom-scraper to 4 replicas now, that's low-risk. ben, can you run rolling restart on node-exporter for gpu-prod-2?
ben: on it. kubectl commands: ```kubectl -n monitoring scale deploy/prom-scraper --replicas=4 && kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart daemonset/node-exporter --selector=nodepool=gpu-prod-2```
dave: running `kubectl get pods -n monitoring -o wide | grep node-exporter` shows pod IPs matching failed nodes. Restarting now.
ops-bot: prom-scraper scaled up to 4 replicas (deployment/prom-scraper). New pod ids: prom-scraper-5, prom-scraper-6.
ben: node-exporter daemonset restart triggered; new pods initializing. Will watch node readiness.
alice: updating PD incident note: mitigation actions started — scaling prom-scraper and restarting node-exporter on gpu-prod-2. No customer SLA breaches observed at this time.
cara: flagged support with customer-facing team to prepare notice if latencies continue.
dave: quick check — after restart, several node-exporter endpoints return 200 for /metrics. Example: `curl -sS https://10.2.14.7:443/metrics | head -n 5` returns prometheus metrics header.
ops-bot: prometheus target status: previously 42 DOWN -> now 10 DOWN, 32 UP (after 2m). scrape_failure_ratio alert trending down.
ben: logs-ingest queue dropping: queue length back to 140, and write-latency down to 9s.
alice: good. I'll hold the page and monitor for 15m. If it stays stable, we'll resolve. Any action items?
cara: file follow-up: investigate kernel OOM frequency on gpu-prod-2 and add a restart policy or resource limits for node-exporter; also add scrapes-per-node alert threshold so we catch before PagerDuty.
dave: +1. I'll open a ticket with node-team and add heap snapshots if we see further OOMs.
alice: handoff: I'm handing to ben for the 10:30 check — if anything flares, escalate to SRE lead.
ben: acknowledged, I'll keep watching dashboards and patch runbooks for node-exporter restarts.
incident-bot: PagerDuty PD-14: acknowledged by alice at 10:12Z. Auto-escalation canceled.
alice: closing the Slack thread — will post postmortem link when ticket is created. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
